items.title: John Abercrombie interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 19, 2001
items.q: and then finally Jack formed a band with myself and Alex Foster, a saxophone player, and Mike Richmond on bass. And we toured for a while as a band

ctx.x: That’s really interesting how names get passed around and people just call you because—

It’s all word of mouth. Yeah. He didn’t know what I played like, but he knew someone had mentioned my name to someone and they mentioned it to Jack and he was looking to start a band and try to do something. He wasn’t playing with Miles anymore. He was kind of on his own. And as a matter of fact one time we had a band with myself and Mick Goodrick, also a great guitar player, and Ron McClure. And then we had a band with Clint Houston, a bass player, and then finally Jack formed a band with myself and Alex Foster,…
Yeah. I love — the critics sometimes let their personal feelings show. This one fellow said, from the CD Guide to Jazz, he says, “John is cited, or blamed, for helping create the ECM sound.”

items.title: Jack DeJohnette — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: my first band had John Abercrombie

ctx.x: Yeah. We did one more record, and actually there was an instrumental that I wrote called “Festival” that CBS wanted to push as a single, but again we had no money to go out and tour. So at that point I said “Okay I’m gonna go sink or swim with jazz.” They let us out of the contract, and I went back to deciding to be a bandleader and I think

my first band had John Abercrombie… I had been working with a group with John and Mick Goodrick; master guitarist and educator who teaches at Berklee. I had the two guitars and a bassist named Clint Houston. So I called on John. John had been working with Chico Hamilton, and so John played spacy guitar and could go a lot of places I wanted to go. (He) had a sense of humor. So, I think that first bass player was named Peter Warren at the time. I was looking for a saxophone player and I think that Alex Foster was…

items.title: Jack DeJohnette interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 7, 2025
items.q: And a lot of prominent musicians came to play there you know — Chick — he told Anthony Braxton, John Abercrombie, Colin Wolcott.

ctx.x: No. Okay. This is a misnomer then.

Yeah, no. She, you know we helped him you know when they were having some financial problems, Lydia and I — or Lydia arranged and shall we say fundraised the concert. And a lot of prominent musicians came to play there you know — Chick — he told Anthony Braxton, John Abercrombie, Colin Wolcott. So you know that’s where the contribution is — a contribution of giving like a free concert to raise money for CMS. But we were never on a board or anything like that. CMS had their own people doing that, managing the place.

What effect do you think your piano skills have on your approach to drumming, or perhaps vice versa. There’s been a number of drummers who play piano and you’re the most prominent one I can think of, and I wonder how those two things work together, if they effect one another?
